images.title: Angle is the turn
images.purpose: The size of an angle depends on the turn between the arms, not on how long the arms are.
images.composition: Two angles of exactly the same opening side by side, one with short arms and one with long arms.
images.exact_structure: Left: one angle of 2 short straight arms in teal #0072B2 with a small arc at the joint. Right: one angle of 2 long straight arms in teal #0072B2 with exactly the same opening and the same arc. Joint dots at the vertices. Exactly 2 angles, 2 arcs.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered

any of the following: two angles with different openings
images.takeaway: Longer arms do not make a bigger angle; only the turn matters.
images.description: Two angles with exactly the same opening: one with short arms and one with long arms, both teal, labelled same angle.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the arc on each angle and say why the two are the same size.

image_decisions.why: The idea that arm length does not change the angle is one clean picture of two equal openings.
